properties.name: Condición de Rango de Cointegración VECM
properties.definition: Supuesto de que la matriz de impacto Pi tiene rango reducido 0 < r < K, garantizando la existencia de r relaciones de equilibrio cointegradas.

properties.name: Exclusion Restriction (Restricción de Exclusión)
properties.definition: Exige que el instrumento z no tenga efecto directo sobre la variable dependiente y excepto a través de su impacto en el regresor endógeno: Cov(z, u) = 0.

reference.book: Introduction to Econometrics with R (Hanck et al.)

properties.name: Supuestos de Gauss-Markov (RLM.1 a RLM.5)
properties.description: Conjunto de cinco supuestos necesarios para que el teorema de Gauss-Markov sea válido en el análisis de regresión múltiple.

properties.name: Identificación Global de Momentos GMM
properties.definition: Condición que exige que E[g(W, theta)] = 0 si y solo si theta = theta_0, junto con el supuesto de que la matriz Jacobiana E[d/dtheta g(W, theta_0)] tiene rango pleno de columnas.

properties.name: Homoscedasticity (Gauss-Markov)
properties.definition: Supuesto clásico de varianza constante condicional de las perturbaciones: Var(u_i | X_i) = sigma^2.

reference.book: Introduction to Econometrics with R (Hanck et al.)
reference.chapter: Chapter 5: Hypothesis Tests in Simple Linear Regression

properties.name: Conditional Ignorability / Exchangeability
properties.definition: Supuesto fundamental de que, condicionado a las covariables medidas X, la asignación del tratamiento es independiente de los resultados potenciales: (Y(1), Y(0)) ⊥ A | X.

reference.book: Fundamentals of causal inference using R (Brumback)

properties.name: Instrument Relevance (Relevancia del Instrumento)
properties.definition: Condición de primer estadio en Variables Instrumentales que exige Cov(z, x | W) != 0, verificada formalmente con un estadístico F de primer estadio > 10.

reference.book: Introduction to Econometrics with R (Hanck et al.)

properties.name: Monotonía en Instrumentos (Monotonicity / No-Defiers)
properties.definition: Supuesto de Angrist e Imbens que establece que la asignación del instrumento afecta el tratamiento en la misma dirección para todos los individuos: D_i(1) >= D_i(0) para todo i (prohibiendo la existencia de Defiers).

properties.name: Condición de Ortogonalidad de Neyman del Score
properties.definition: Supuesto estructural que exige que la función de momentos psi sea de Neyman-ortogonal respecto a las funciones nuisance poblacionales: d/d_eta E[psi(W; theta_0, eta_0)] = 0.

properties.name: No Perfect Multicollinearity (Gauss-Markov)
properties.definition: Exige que ninguna variable explicativa sea combinación lineal exacta de otras covariables, garantizando rank(X) = k + 1.

reference.book: Introduction to Econometrics with R (Hanck et al.)

properties.name: Parallel Trends (Diferencias-en-Diferencias)
properties.definition: Supuesto contrafáctico de que, en ausencia de intervención, la trayectoria temporal media del resultado en el grupo tratado habría evolucionado en paralelo a la del grupo de control.

reference.book: Introduction to Econometrics with R (Hanck et al.)

properties.name: Positivity / Overlap
properties.definition: Condición según la cual todo individuo tiene probabilidad estrictamente positiva y no unitaria de recibir cualquier nivel de tratamiento dado su conjunto de covariables: 0 < P(A=1|X) < 1.

reference.book: Fundamentals of causal inference using R (Brumback)

properties.name: Monotonía Estricta en Regresión Cuantílica
properties.definition: Supuesto de que la función de distribución acumulada condicional F_Y|X(y|x) es estrictamente monótona creciente y continuamente diferenciable en el soporte de Y.

properties.name: Strict Exogeneity in Panel Data
properties.definition: Condición E[u_it | X_i1, ..., X_iT, c_i] = 0 que exige que los errores transitorios sean ortogonales a las covariables en todos los periodos pasados, presentes y futuros.

reference.book: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data (Wooldridge)
reference.chapter: Chapter 10: Basic Linear Unobserved Effects Panel Data Models

properties.name: SUTVA (Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption)
properties.definition: Supuesto que estipula dos condiciones: 1) No interferencia (el tratamiento de una unidad no afecta los resultados de otras), y 2) No variaciones ocultas en la dosis del tratamiento.

reference.book: Fundamentals of causal inference using R (Brumback)
reference.chapter: Chapter 3: The SUTVA Assumption in Causal Inference

properties.name: Ortogonalidad Contemporánea de Shocks Estructurales
properties.definition: Supuesto de que los shocks estructurales son mutuamente incorrelados y presentan matriz de varianzas-covarianzas diagonal o normalizada a la identidad: E[eps_t eps_t'] = I_K.

properties.name: Stationarity & Absence of Unit Roots
properties.definition: Condición de que las raíces de la ecuación característica autorregresiva se encuentren estrictamente fuera del círculo unitario (|z| > 1).

reference.book: Time Series Analysis with Applications in R (Cryer & Chan)
reference.chapter: Chapter 4: Models for Stationary Time Series

properties.name: Usar muestras grandes para mayor precisión
properties.description: Una varianza grande del error puede ser contrarrestada con un tamaño de muestra grande, permitiendo estimar con precisión los efectos parciales.
properties.rationale: Más datos ayudan a reducir el error estándar de los estimadores, incluso si R2 es pequeño.

properties.name: Evaluate ROC Curves on Test Data
properties.description: Always compute ROC curves on test data to assess prediction accuracy, not just on training data.
properties.rationale: Training data may overestimate accuracy; test data provides a realistic measure.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evaluate ROC on Test Data
properties.description: ROC curves should be computed on test data to assess prediction accuracy, not just on training data.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Separate Training and Testing Data
properties.description: Always train and test models on separate data sets to avoid overfitting and obtain unbiased performance estimates.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: Lab: Logistic Regression, LDA, QDA, and KNN

properties.name: Add Interaction Terms to GAM
properties.description: Manually include interaction terms or low-dimensional interaction functions in GAMs to capture important variable interactions.
properties.rationale: GAMs are additive by default and may miss interactions unless explicitly included.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Add Interaction Terms to GAMs
properties.description: Manually include interaction terms or low-dimensional interaction functions in GAMs to capture important joint effects between variables.
properties.rationale: GAMs are additive by default and may miss interactions unless specified.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Add Interaction Terms to GAM
properties.description: Manually include interaction terms or low-dimensional interaction functions in a GAM to capture important variable interactions that the additive model may miss.
properties.rationale: GAMs are additive by default and may miss interactions unless specified.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Add Quadratic Terms for Significant Variables
properties.description: It is recommended to add quadratic terms for significant variables and perform a joint significance test to detect non-linear relationships.

properties.name: Ajustar valores ajustados fuera del intervalo unitario
properties.description: Cuando los valores ajustados están fuera del intervalo [0,1], se recomienda ajustarlos antes de aplicar MCP.
properties.rationale: Evita ponderadores negativos o cero y mejora la validez de la estimación.

properties.name: Adjust for Batch Effects
properties.description: It is recommended to account for batch effects (such as machine or day) before comparing experimental groups.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Adjust for Confounding Variables in Regression
properties.description: Always include relevant predictors to avoid misleading associations caused by confounding variables.
properties.rationale: Simple regression may attribute effects to a variable due to correlation with another predictor.
examples: Newspaper advertising appears to affect sales due to correlation with radio advertising.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Adjust Logistic Regression Probability Cutoff
properties.description: Lowering the probability cutoff in logistic regression can improve the detection of positive cases in imbalanced datasets.
properties.rationale: A default cutoff of 0.5 may miss most positives when the outcome is rare.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Adjust ntree argument for performance
properties.description: The number of trees grown in randomForest() can be changed using the ntree argument to balance computation and accuracy.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Adjust Probability Cutoff in Logistic Regression
properties.description: Lower the probability threshold below 0.5 to improve recall for rare positive classes in imbalanced datasets.
properties.rationale: Default cutoff may miss all positives; lowering increases true positives.
examples: Cutoff at 0.25 yields 33% success rate vs. 0% at 0.5.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Ajustar errores estándar por correlación serial
properties.description: Es necesario ajustar los errores estándar cuando los errores presentan correlación serial.

properties.name: Agrupar categorías de variables altamente correlacionadas
properties.description: Es preferible agrupar categorías de gastos altamente correlacionadas en lugar de estimar el efecto de cada una por separado.
properties.rationale: Esto evita problemas de multicolinealidad autoimpuestos y mejora la precisión del análisis.

properties.name: Usar R-cuadrada basada en serie sin estacionalidad
properties.description: Cuando la serie tiene estacionalidad pronunciada, es mejor medir el ajuste usando la R-cuadrada de la serie ajustada por estacionalidad.

properties.name: Allow Random Regressors in Asymptotic Analysis
properties.description: Permitting random explanatory variables simplifies asymptotic analysis and avoids unrealistic restrictions.
properties.rationale: Fixed regressor assumption can impose unintended restrictions and is often unrealistic in social science applications.

reference.book: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data

properties.name: Analizar observaciones aberrantes
properties.description: Es recomendable revisar las observaciones para identificar aquellas que pueden tener una influencia sustancial sobre las estimaciones de MCO.
properties.rationale: Observaciones aberrantes pueden distorsionar los resultados y reducir la validez del análisis.

properties.name: Aplicar varios métodos econométricos
properties.description: Comparar resultados obtenidos con diferentes métodos para identificar supuestos posiblemente incorrectos.

properties.name: Referenciar comandos especiales en apéndice
properties.description: Los comandos del paquete de econometría que no son relevantes para el análisis principal deben referirse a un apéndice.
properties.rationale: Evita sobrecargar el reporte principal y permite documentar detalles técnicos.

properties.name: Assess Cluster Robustness
properties.description: Check if clusters remain similar when data is perturbed or subsets are removed, as clustering methods are often not robust.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Attach dataset for variable access
properties.description: Use attach() to make dataset variables accessible by name in R.
properties.rationale: Allows direct access to variables without specifying the dataset each time.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evitar decir 'se acepta H0'
properties.description: Se recomienda decir 'no se puede rechazar H0 al nivel de x%' en vez de 'se acepta H0', ya que pueden existir múltiples hipótesis no rechazadas simultáneamente.

properties.name: Avoid Best Subset Selection with Large p
properties.description: Best subset selection is computationally infeasible and prone to overfitting when the number of predictors is large.
properties.rationale: The search space grows exponentially with p, increasing computation time and the risk of finding spurious models.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Classical Methods in High Dimensions
properties.description: Classical approaches like least squares regression should not be used when the number of features is as large as or larger than the number of observations.
properties.rationale: These methods will always yield a perfect fit with zero residuals, regardless of any true relationship.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.4.2 What Goes Wrong in High Dimensions?

properties.name: Avoid High Cost to Prevent Overfitting in SVM
properties.description: Using a high cost parameter in SVM can reduce training errors but leads to an irregular decision boundary and overfitting.
properties.rationale: Lower cost allows for wider margin and better generalization.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid High Cost Values in SVM
properties.description: High cost values can reduce training errors but often lead to overfitting and irregular decision boundaries.
properties.rationale: Model may perform poorly on test data due to overfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Misinterpreting Horizontal Proximity in Dendrograms
properties.description: Do not infer similarity between observations solely because they are close on the horizontal axis of a dendrogram.
properties.rationale: There are multiple possible reorderings of leaves; only vertical fusion points matter.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Incorrect Inclusion of Variables
properties.description: Do not include explanatory variables as numeric values in regression models if they lack meaningful interpretation.
properties.rationale: Including meaningless numeric variables can distort model results.

properties.name: Avoid Large Search Spaces in Model Selection
properties.description: Large search spaces increase the risk of overfitting and high variance in coefficient estimates.
properties.rationale: Models selected from enormous search spaces may perform well on training data but lack predictive power on new data.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Least Squares in High-Dimensional Settings
properties.description: Least squares regression should not be performed when the number of features is equal to or greater than the number of observations.
properties.rationale: It will yield a perfect fit to the data, resulting in zero residuals and unreliable coefficient estimates.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.4.2 What Goes Wrong in High Dimensions?

properties.name: Evitar tendencia lineal para pronosticar caminatas aleatorias
properties.description: No se debe utilizar una tendencia lineal para pronosticar una caminata aleatoria con tendencia estocástica, ya que produce errores de pronóstico con varianza creciente.
properties.rationale: La varianza del error de pronóstico es mayor con tendencia lineal comparado con el modelo de caminata aleatoria.

properties.name: Evitar realizar manualmente la segunda etapa de MC2E
properties.description: No se recomienda ejecutar manualmente la segunda etapa de MC2E, ya que los errores estándar y los estadísticos de prueba obtenidos no son válidos.
properties.rationale: El término de error incluye componentes adicionales que no son considerados en los errores estándar convencionales.

properties.name: Avoid Naive Error Metrics in High Dimensions
properties.description: Do not rely solely on sum of squared errors, p-values, or R2 when p > n, as these can be misleading in high-dimensional settings.
properties.rationale: It is possible to obtain models with zero residuals that are not predictive.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Negative Probabilities in Confidence Intervals
properties.description: When computing confidence intervals for probabilities in logistic regression, always calculate intervals on the logit scale before transforming to the probability scale.
properties.rationale: Direct calculation on the probability scale can result in negative probabilities, which are not meaningful.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evitar controlar demasiados factores en regresión
properties.description: No se deben incluir demasiadas variables en un modelo de regresión solo para mejorar la bondad de ajuste.
properties.rationale: Controlar factores irrelevantes puede distorsionar la interpretación ceteris paribus y reducir la validez del modelo.

properties.name: Avoid Overfitting in Decision Trees
properties.description: Prune the tree or set a stopping criterion to prevent the model from becoming too complex and overfitting the training data.
properties.rationale: Overly complex trees may fit the training data well but perform poorly on new data.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Overfitting with High Gamma in SVM
properties.description: A high gamma value in SVM with RBF kernel can lead to overfitting, resulting in poor test performance.
properties.rationale: Lower training error does not guarantee improved test performance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 9.4 SVMs with More than Two Classes

properties.name: Avoid Overfitting with Flexible Models
properties.description: More flexible models may achieve lower training error but do not necessarily perform better on test data.
properties.rationale: Overfitting leads to poor generalization and worse performance on unseen data.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 9.4 SVMs with More than Two Classes

properties.name: Evitar comparar R-cuadrada entre diferentes transformaciones de la variable dependiente
properties.description: No se debe usar R-cuadrada ni R-cuadrada ajustada para comparar modelos con distintas formas funcionales de la variable dependiente.
properties.rationale: La variación total de y y de log(y) es diferente, lo que invalida la comparación.

properties.name: Avoid Standard Metrics in High Dimensions
properties.description: Standard metrics such as sum of squared errors, p-values, and R2 should not be used when p > n due to risk of misleading results.
properties.rationale: High-dimensional models can fit training data perfectly, resulting in zero residuals and invalid statistical measures.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid using training error for model selection
properties.description: Selecting models based solely on training error (low RSS or high R2) can lead to overfitting; use test error or cross-validation instead.
properties.rationale: Training error underestimates the true prediction error and does not guarantee good test performance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Using Training Error for Model Selection
properties.description: Selecting models based on training error (RSS or R2) can lead to overfitting; use test error or cross-validation instead.
properties.rationale: Training error tends to be much smaller than test error and does not guarantee good generalization.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid Uncentered R-squared
properties.description: Do not use uncentered R-squared as a measure of fit; it can be artificially high and misleading.
properties.rationale: Centered R-squared is more informative and accurate.

properties.name: Avoid unnecessary high-degree polynomial regression
properties.description: Higher-order polynomial models may not be justified and can lead to overfitting; use cubic or quartic only if supported by statistical tests.
properties.rationale: Degree-5 polynomial was unnecessary as indicated by high p-value.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Avoid using individual p-values for overall association
properties.description: Do not rely on individual p-values to determine if any predictor is associated with the response when many predictors are present.
properties.rationale: High risk of false positives due to multiple testing.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Avoid Using Training Error for Model Selection
properties.description: Selecting models based solely on training error (RSS or R2) leads to overfitting; prefer cross-validated prediction error or penalized criteria.
properties.rationale: Training error underestimates test error and does not guarantee good generalization.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Backward Stepwise Selection requires n > p
properties.description: Backward stepwise selection can only be applied when the number of samples exceeds the number of predictors.
properties.rationale: The full model cannot be fit if there are more predictors than samples.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Binary Variables for Qualitative Factors
properties.description: Include binary variables to represent qualitative attributes or groups in regression models.
properties.rationale: Binary variables allow qualitative factors to be incorporated into quantitative models.

properties.name: Tune shrinkage parameter in boosting
properties.description: Adjusting the shrinkage parameter λ in boosting can improve test MSE.
properties.rationale: Different values of λ affect model performance; smaller or larger values may yield better results.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Bootstrap for Standard Error Estimation
properties.description: Bootstrap provides more accurate standard error estimates when model assumptions are violated.
properties.rationale: Bootstrap does not rely on assumptions about fixed predictors or correct model specification.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Bootstrap for More Accurate Standard Errors
properties.description: Bootstrap estimates of standard errors do not rely on model assumptions and can be more accurate than standard formulas.
properties.rationale: Standard formulas depend on assumptions about the noise variance and fixed predictors, which bootstrap does not.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Bootstrap for Standard Error Estimation
properties.description: Bootstrap does not rely on assumptions about fixed predictors or correct model specification, making it more robust for estimating standard errors.
properties.rationale: Standard formulas depend on assumptions that may not hold in real data, inflating error estimates.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Preferir bootstrap cuando la fórmula analítica es compleja
properties.description: El uso de bootstrap facilita el cálculo de errores estándar en comparación con obtener una fórmula analítica para el error estándar asintótico.
properties.rationale: Bootstrap requiere menos trabajo computacional y es más flexible.

properties.name: Calcular errores estándar robustos en MCP
properties.description: Siempre calcular errores estándar y estadísticos de prueba robustos tras estimar por MCP, ya que la función de la varianza puede estar mal especificada.
properties.rationale: Los errores estándar usuales de MCP pueden ser inválidos si la función de varianza es incorrecta.

properties.name: Calcular estadísticos de resumen para detectar errores
properties.description: Siempre es aconsejable calcular mínimos y máximos para evitar errores en el registro de los datos.
properties.rationale: Errores al registrar datos pueden afectar gravemente las estimaciones de MCO, especialmente en muestras pequeñas.

properties.name: Cálculo alternativo de R2 en regresión a través del origen
properties.description: Para evitar valores negativos de R2, se recomienda calcular R2 como el cuadrado del coeficiente de correlación entre los valores reales y los ajustados de y.

properties.name: Cálculo de varianza
properties.description: Para calcular la varianza, primero se obtiene el valor esperado y luego el valor esperado del cuadrado de la variable.
properties.rationale: Este método es aplicable tanto para variables discretas como continuas.

properties.name: Careful Causality Inference
properties.description: Avoid inferring causality without proper controls and model specification, especially in observational studies.
properties.rationale: Causal inference requires accounting for confounding variables and proper econometric techniques.

properties.name: Transformar datos con cuidado
properties.description: Revise la estructura y el orden de los datos antes de aplicar transformaciones, especialmente en series de tiempo.
properties.rationale: Errores en la transformación pueden llevar a resultados incorrectos.

properties.name: Cuidado al sustituir combinaciones de variables dummy
properties.description: Al interpretar modelos con múltiples variables dummy e interacciones, es fundamental usar correctamente las combinaciones de ceros y unos para identificar los grupos.

properties.name: Be cautious with long-term forecasts using trend models
properties.description: Trend models should be used carefully for long-term forecasts, especially for integrated series with stochastic trends.
properties.rationale: Forecasts may be unreliable when projecting far into the future due to stochastic components.

properties.name: Apply Careful Model Selection
properties.description: Avoid selecting models based solely on training R2 or MSE, especially in high-dimensional settings, to prevent overfitting.
properties.rationale: High training R2 or low training MSE can be misleading when the number of features is large.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Careful Outlier Removal
properties.description: Remove outliers only if they are due to data collection or recording errors; otherwise, they may indicate a model deficiency such as a missing predictor.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 3.3 Other Considerations in the Regression Model

properties.name: Cuidado al exponenciar pronósticos log-lineales
properties.description: No se debe simplemente exponenciar el pronóstico de log(yt) para obtener el pronóstico de yt; se debe considerar el error implícito.
properties.rationale: Ignorar el error lleva a pronósticos sesgados.

properties.name: Cautious Reporting in High-Dimensional Settings
properties.description: Be careful when reporting errors and measures of model fit in high-dimensional settings, as traditional metrics can be misleading.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Center and Scale Variables Before PCA
properties.description: Variables should be centered to mean zero and scaled to unit variance before performing PCA to ensure meaningful results.
properties.rationale: Scaling affects PCA results, unlike linear regression where scaling has no substantive effect.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Center and Scale Variables Before PCA
properties.description: Variables should be centered to mean zero and scaled to standard deviation one before performing PCA to ensure meaningful results.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Center Variables Before PCA
properties.description: Variables should be centered to have mean zero before performing PCA to ensure meaningful results.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Centrar variables antes de crear términos de interacción
properties.description: Sustraer la media de las variables explicativas antes de crear el término de interacción facilita la interpretación de los coeficientes.
properties.rationale: Permite que los coeficientes de las variables originales representen efectos parciales en valores útiles, como la media.

properties.name: Center and Scale Variables Before PCA
properties.description: Variables should be centered to mean zero and often scaled to have unit variance before performing PCA.
properties.rationale: PCA results depend on the scale of the variables; unscaled variables can distort the principal components.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Center Variables Before PCA
properties.description: Variables should be centered to have mean zero before performing PCA to ensure meaningful results.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Check Number of Clusters
properties.description: Always consider different values of K in K-means clustering, as the true number of clusters is usually unknown in real data.
properties.rationale: Incorrect K can lead to misleading cluster assignments.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Check Cluster Robustness
properties.description: Assess how clustering results change when data is perturbed or subsets are removed.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Check Confidence Intervals with Response Type
properties.description: Avoid calculating confidence intervals on predicted probabilities using type='response' in predict(), as this can yield nonsensical (e.g., negative) probabilities.
properties.rationale: The transformation can distort the interval, leading to invalid probability values.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: View data before loading into R
properties.description: It is recommended to inspect data files in a text editor or Excel before loading them into R to check for issues such as missing values or incorrect headers.
properties.rationale: Prevents errors during data import and ensures correct interpretation of variable names and missing values.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Check OLS Assumptions
properties.description: Justify the use of OLS by ensuring key assumptions, such as no correlation between errors and regressors, are satisfied.
properties.rationale: Violating OLS assumptions can lead to biased or inconsistent estimates.

properties.name: Verificar sensibilidad a observaciones atípicas
properties.description: Es importante analizar la influencia de observaciones atípicas en los resultados de regresión, especialmente con MCO.
properties.rationale: Observaciones influyentes pueden distorsionar las estimaciones.

properties.name: Check p-values for predictors
properties.description: Always examine p-values to assess the statistical significance of predictors in logistic regression.
properties.rationale: High p-values indicate weak evidence of association.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 4.6 Lab: Logistic Regression, LDA, QDA, and KNN

properties.name: Check Residual Patterns for Correlation
properties.description: Plot residuals as a function of time to detect correlation among error terms, especially in time series data.
properties.rationale: Correlated errors can lead to underestimated standard errors and misleading inference.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Check Robustness of Clustering
properties.description: Clustering results may change with data perturbations; always check robustness.
properties.rationale: Removing random subsets of data can lead to different clusters.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Verificar ajuste estacional en variables de series de tiempo
properties.description: Determine si las variables han sido ajustadas estacionalmente cuando se usan datos mensuales o trimestrales.
properties.rationale: El ajuste estacional afecta la interpretación y el análisis de los datos.

properties.name: Check Serial Correlation in Errors
properties.description: Testing for serial correlation in error terms is important for choosing between fixed effects and first difference estimators.
properties.rationale: Efficiency of estimators depends on the presence and direction of serial correlation.

properties.name: Verificar el orden cronológico en series de tiempo
properties.description: Asegúrese de que los datos de series de tiempo estén ordenados del periodo más antiguo al más reciente antes de realizar transformaciones como diferencias.
properties.rationale: El desorden en los datos puede generar resultados inservibles al calcular cambios entre periodos.

properties.name: Verificar unidades de medición
properties.description: Es importante saber cómo se miden las variables para interpretar correctamente los resultados de regresión.
properties.rationale: Cambios en las unidades de medición afectan las estimaciones obtenidas.

properties.name: Verificar la naturaleza de las variables
properties.description: Identifique si las variables son binarias, ordinales, sus unidades de medida y si están expresadas en términos nominales o reales.
properties.rationale: Permite interpretar correctamente los datos y evitar errores en el análisis.

properties.name: Choose Polynomial Degree via Cross-Validation
properties.description: Selecting the degree of the polynomial using cross-validation is preferable to solely relying on hypothesis tests or ANOVA.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choose Dissimilarity Measure Carefully
properties.description: The choice of dissimilarity measure in hierarchical clustering should be guided by the data type and scientific question, as it strongly affects the resulting clusters.
properties.rationale: Inappropriate measures can lead to misleading clusters, such as grouping infrequent users together.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Careful Selection of K in KNN
properties.description: Selecting the appropriate value of K is crucial for KNN performance, especially with complex non-linear data.
properties.rationale: Too low K can lead to overfitting; too high K can lead to underfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Careful Selection of K in KNN
properties.description: Choosing the correct level of smoothness (K) in KNN is crucial, as too low K can lead to poor results even in complex non-linear data.
properties.rationale: KNN with K=1 performed worst in the scenario, highlighting the importance of selecting K appropriately.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choose Lambda via Cross-Validation
properties.description: Selecting the regularization parameter lambda using cross-validation is preferable to arbitrary selection.
properties.rationale: Cross-validation provides an unbiased estimate of test error and helps avoid overfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choose Linkage Method Carefully
properties.description: Selecting an appropriate linkage method (complete, average, single) affects cluster results and interpretation.
properties.rationale: Different linkage methods may produce varying cluster assignments, with single linkage prone to chaining effects.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choose number of principal components by cross-validation in PCR
properties.description: Select the number of principal components (M) in PCR using cross-validation to minimize prediction error.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choose an appropriate number of principal components (M) in PCR
properties.description: Selecting the right number of principal components can substantially improve prediction accuracy and minimize mean squared error.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choose Optimal K in KNN
properties.description: Selecting an appropriate value for K is crucial; too low leads to high variance and overfitting, too high leads to high bias and underfitting.
properties.rationale: Optimal K minimizes test error and balances bias and variance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Careful Selection of Smoothness in KNN
properties.description: The value of K in KNN must be chosen carefully to balance bias and variance and avoid poor classification performance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: La prueba de Chow requiere homocedasticidad
properties.description: La prueba de Chow solo es válida si las varianzas del error son iguales en ambos grupos.
properties.rationale: La heteroscedasticidad invalida la prueba F utilizada en la prueba de Chow.

properties.name: Order Panel Data Chronologically
properties.description: Panel data should be ordered chronologically within each cross-sectional unit before differentiation to avoid errors.
properties.rationale: Improper ordering can create nonsensical observations when differencing data.

properties.name: Store time series data in chronological order
properties.description: Time series data should be entered and stored chronologically, with the oldest period as the first observation and the most recent as the last.
properties.rationale: Ensures correct analysis and interpretation of temporal patterns.

properties.name: Reportar resultados en tablas claras
properties.description: Las tablas deben indicar claramente las variables dependientes e independientes, y especificar si se reportan errores estándar o estadísticos t bajo los coeficientes.
properties.rationale: Facilita la interpretación y comparación de modelos.

properties.name: Use Clustering as Hypothesis Generation
properties.description: Treat clustering results as a starting point for scientific hypotheses and further study, not as absolute truth.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Careful Reporting of Clustering Results
properties.description: Clustering results should be reported as a starting point for scientific hypothesis development, not as absolute truth.
properties.rationale: Results may not generalize and should be validated on independent data sets.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Assess Clustering Robustness
properties.description: Perform clustering with different parameter choices and on subsets of data to evaluate the robustness of clusters.
properties.rationale: Clustering can be non-robust and sensitive to preprocessing choices.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Combine Collinear Variables
properties.description: Combine collinear variables into a single predictor, such as by averaging standardized versions, to address collinearity.
properties.rationale: Combining variables reduces collinearity and can create a more meaningful predictor.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Comparar coeficientes entre logit, probit y MPL usando factores escalares
properties.description: Para comparar magnitudes de coeficientes entre modelos logit, probit y MPL, multiplique los coeficientes probit por 1.6 o los logit por 0.625. Para comparar logit con MPL, divida los coeficientes logit entre 4 y los probit entre 2.5.

properties.name: Compare results across estimation methods
properties.description: Comment on critical differences when using methods like OLS, 2SLS, or panel data.

properties.name: Compare models using test set MSE
properties.description: Evaluate and compare different models by computing their mean squared error on the test set.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.6 Lab 2: Ridge Regression and the Lasso

properties.name: Compare Models Using Test MSE
properties.description: Evaluate and compare models based on their mean squared error on the test set.
properties.rationale: Test MSE provides an unbiased estimate of model performance on unseen data.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.6 Lab 2: Ridge Regression and the Lasso

properties.name: Compare Multiple Model Selection Criteria
properties.description: Evaluate models using several criteria such as adjusted R2, Cp, and BIC to make a robust selection.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Comparar estimaciones de MCO, EF y EA
properties.description: Es recomendable comparar los resultados de MCO combinados, efectos fijos y efectos aleatorios para evaluar la naturaleza de los sesgos y la importancia de los efectos inobservables.

properties.name: Compare R-squared Between Log and Linear Models
properties.description: Use the squared correlation between actual and predicted values to compare the fit of log-transformed and linear models.
properties.rationale: Allows direct comparison of model fit regardless of transformation.

properties.name: Compare Training, Test, and Cross-validation Errors
properties.description: Evaluating all three error rates helps assess model performance and avoid overfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Compare Training and Test Error Rates
properties.description: Always evaluate both training and test error rates, as test error rates are the real measure of model performance.
properties.rationale: Training error rates are often lower due to parameter adjustment and may not reflect real-world performance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Consider Outliers in Clustering
properties.description: Use mixture models or other approaches to accommodate outliers that do not belong to any cluster.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Formato consistente de filas en archivos de datos
properties.description: Cada fila debe comenzar con una nueva observación, contener el mismo orden de variables y el mismo número de entradas, y los valores deben estar separados por al menos un espacio.

properties.name: Controlar antecedentes familiares en regresión
properties.description: Incluir variables de antecedentes familiares en la regresión ayuda a obtener estimadores insesgados del efecto del tratamiento si estas variables están correlacionadas con la variable dependiente.

properties.name: Control Unobserved Effects with Dummies
properties.description: It is better to treat individual effects as omitted variables controlled by within transformation rather than estimating them directly.

properties.name: Controlar factores omitidos usando valores rezagados
properties.description: Incluir valores rezagados de la variable dependiente puede ayudar a obtener mejores estimaciones de efectos ceteris paribus.
properties.rationale: Ayuda a controlar variables no observadas que afectan el resultado.

properties.name: Convert numeric variable to factor for boxplots
properties.description: Convert numeric variables with few distinct values to factors to produce boxplots.
properties.rationale: Boxplots are automatically produced when the x-axis variable is categorical.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Convertir porcentajes a proporciones antes de calcular
properties.description: Siempre convierta porcentajes a proporciones decimales antes de realizar cálculos para evitar errores.
properties.rationale: Multiplicar directamente por el porcentaje puede llevar a resultados incorrectos.
examples: Intereses sobre $3,000 a 7.6% se calcula como 3,000 x 0.076, no 3,000 x 7.6

properties.name: Use cor() only with numeric variables
properties.description: The cor() function in R requires all input variables to be numeric; qualitative variables will cause errors.
properties.rationale: cor() cannot compute correlations for non-numeric data.
common_errors: Error in cor(Smarket): 'x' must be numeric

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 4.6 Lab: Logistic Regression, LDA, QDA, and KNN

properties.name: Select Number of Components via Cross-Validation
properties.description: Cross-validation should be used to determine the optimal number of principal components for PCR.
properties.rationale: Ensures the model balances bias and variance for best predictive performance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation to Select Number of Principal Components in Supervised Analysis
properties.description: When using principal components in supervised learning, treat the number of components as a tuning parameter and select it via cross-validation.
properties.rationale: Provides an objective and data-driven method for component selection in supervised contexts.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation to Select Lambda
properties.description: Instead of arbitrarily choosing lambda, use cross-validation to select the value that minimizes prediction error.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation for Model Selection
properties.description: Cross-validation helps select optimal model parameters, such as polynomial degree or degrees of freedom in splines, by evaluating predictive performance.
properties.rationale: Reduces risk of overfitting and ensures generalizability.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-validation for Parameter Selection
properties.description: Cross-validation should be used to select optimal values for SVM parameters such as cost, gamma, and degree.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation to Choose Span
properties.description: Cross-validation can be used to select the span parameter for local regression to balance fit flexibility and smoothness.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation to Select Number of Principal Components in Supervised Analysis
properties.description: When using principal components in a supervised analysis, treat the number of components as a tuning parameter and select it via cross-validation.
properties.rationale: Provides an objective and well-defined method for component selection.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Cross-Validation for Principal Components Regression
properties.description: In supervised analysis, the number of principal components to use can be objectively selected via cross-validation.
properties.rationale: Supervised analyses allow for objective evaluation using tuning parameters.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use cross-validation to select number of components in PCR
properties.description: Apply cross-validation to determine the optimal number of principal components for PCR, minimizing prediction error.
properties.rationale: Choosing too many or too few components can lead to underfitting or overfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation for Tree Pruning
properties.description: Cross-validation helps determine the optimal tree size and whether pruning improves test error.
properties.rationale: Pruning can reduce overfitting and improve generalization.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Customize plots with options
properties.description: Use options like col, varwidth, horizontal, xlab, and ylab to tailor plots for better visualization.
examples: plot(cylinders, mpg, col='red', varwidth=TRUE, horizontal=TRUE, xlab='cylinders', ylab='MPG')

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Specify breaks in cut()
properties.description: Use the breaks option in cut() to manually define bin edges for more control over interval boundaries.
properties.rationale: Allows customization of groupings to fit the data or analysis goals.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Ordenar datos de panel para diferenciación
properties.description: Los datos deben organizarse por unidad y en orden cronológico antes de calcular primeras diferencias.
properties.rationale: Facilita el cálculo correcto de diferencias y evita errores en el análisis.

properties.name: Report Data Sources Clearly
properties.description: Include all applicable public data sources and list scarce datasets in the appendix.
properties.rationale: Ensures reproducibility and transparency for other researchers.

properties.name: Plantear una pregunta específica
properties.description: Definir claramente la meta del análisis empírico para evitar errores en la recolección de datos y selección de variables.
properties.rationale: Sin una pregunta bien formulada, se pueden omitir variables importantes o usar muestras inadecuadas.

properties.name: Select Polynomial Degree Carefully
properties.description: Choose the degree of the polynomial based on hypothesis tests to avoid overfitting and ensure model simplicity.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Avoid Interpreting Horizontal Proximity in Dendrograms
properties.description: Do not conclude similarity between observations based on their horizontal proximity in a dendrogram.
properties.rationale: There are many possible reorderings of the dendrogram that do not affect cluster meaning.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Interpret Dendrograms by Vertical Axis
properties.description: Similarity between observations in a dendrogram should be inferred from the vertical axis where their branches fuse, not their horizontal proximity.
properties.rationale: Horizontal ordering can be swapped without affecting the meaning of the dendrogram.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Dendrogram Leaf Position Equivalence
properties.description: The position of leaves in a dendrogram can be swapped without changing its meaning, as long as the cluster relationships are preserved.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Dendrogram Leaf Swapping
properties.description: Swapping the position of leaves in a dendrogram does not change its meaning, as cluster fusion order is preserved.
properties.rationale: Cluster relationships remain unchanged regardless of leaf order.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Describe coefficient magnitudes
properties.description: Discuss the magnitudes of coefficients for key explanatory variables.

properties.name: Usar nombres descriptivos para variables dummy
properties.description: Se recomienda asignar nombres claros a las variables dummy para mejorar la claridad de la ecuación y su interpretación.
properties.rationale: Nombres descriptivos facilitan la comprensión y exposición de los resultados.

properties.name: Detect Collinearity in Regression Models
properties.description: Identify and address collinearity problems while fitting regression models to avoid masking the importance of variables.
properties.rationale: Collinearity can inflate standard errors and reduce the power of hypothesis tests.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 3.3 Other Considerations in the Regression Model

properties.name: Diferenciar variables para eliminar correlación serial
properties.description: Tomar la primera diferencia de las variables en una regresión de series de tiempo ayuda a eliminar la correlación serial y posibles raíces unitarias.
properties.rationale: La correlación serial y raíces unitarias pueden invalidar los resultados de MCO; la diferenciación mejora la confianza en los errores estándar.

properties.name: Diferenciar series sospechosas de raíz unitaria
properties.description: Se recomienda obtener la primera diferencia de cualquier serie de tiempo sospechosa de tener raíz unitaria antes de hacer regresiones.
properties.rationale: La diferenciación ayuda a evitar problemas de no estacionariedad y resultados espurios.

properties.name: Differencing Series with High Autocorrelation
properties.description: If the first order autocorrelation is above 0.9 (or 0.8), it is common practice to difference the series to achieve stationarity.
properties.rationale: High autocorrelation suggests a unit root and non-stationarity.

properties.name: Distinguir entre cambio porcentual y puntos porcentuales
properties.description: Es fundamental diferenciar entre cambio porcentual y puntos porcentuales para evitar confusiones en la interpretación de resultados.
properties.rationale: La confusión entre ambos puede llevar a errores en la comunicación de resultados en investigaciones y medios.

properties.name: Distinguish between economic and statistical significance
properties.description: Discuss both the statistical and practical importance of coefficients.
properties.rationale: Statistical significance does not imply practical relevance.

properties.name: Do not say 'accept H0'
properties.description: It is incorrect to say 'accept H0'; instead, say 'do not reject H0' because multiple hypotheses may not be rejected.
properties.rationale: Only one hypothesis can be true, but several may not be rejected.

properties.name: Do Not Remove Principal Component Blindly
properties.description: Avoid subtracting principal components without understanding their source, as this may remove biological signal.
properties.rationale: Principal components may capture both technical and biological variation.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Drop Collinear Variables
properties.description: Remove one of the problematic collinear variables from the regression to reduce redundancy and improve model stability.
properties.rationale: Collinearity implies redundant information, so dropping a variable usually does not compromise the regression fit.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Drop Irrelevant Predictors
properties.description: Exclude predictors that do not significantly improve model fit to avoid unnecessary complexity and overfitting.
properties.rationale: Including weak predictors can lead to overfitting and does not improve predictive accuracy.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Coding of Dummy Variables is Arbitrary
properties.description: The choice of which group is coded as 0 or 1 does not affect the regression fit, but changes coefficient interpretation.
properties.rationale: Interpretation of coefficients depends on coding scheme, but predictions remain the same.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Interpretation of Dummy Variable Coefficients
properties.description: Coefficients for dummy variables should be interpreted as differences from the baseline category, and the coding scheme affects only the interpretation, not the prediction.
properties.rationale: Ensures clarity in understanding model output and avoids misinterpretation.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: Other Considerations in the Regression Model

properties.name: Nombrar variables ficticias claramente
properties.description: Las variables ficticias deben tener nombres que indiquen claramente el grupo al que pertenecen, como 'Dem' para demócratas y 'Rep' para republicanos.
properties.rationale: Evita confusión sobre el significado de los valores de la variable.

properties.name: Analizar significancia económica y estadística
properties.description: Verifique primero la significancia estadística de una variable y luego evalúe la magnitud de su coeficiente para determinar su importancia práctica o económica.
properties.rationale: Una variable puede ser estadísticamente significativa pero no relevante económicamente, o viceversa.

properties.name: Eliminar variables perfectamente colineales
properties.description: Se recomienda eliminar del modelo una de las variables que presentan colinealidad perfecta para evitar problemas de identificación.
properties.rationale: La colinealidad perfecta impide la estimación de los parámetros del modelo.

properties.name: Encode Response as Factor for Classification
properties.description: The response variable must be encoded as a factor in R to perform classification with svm().
properties.rationale: svm() distinguishes between regression and classification based on the response type.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Encode response as factor for classification
properties.description: For the svm() function to perform classification, the response variable must be encoded as a factor.
properties.rationale: svm() distinguishes between classification and regression based on the response type.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Calcular errores estándar robustos
properties.description: Se recomienda calcular errores estándar robustos ante heterocedasticidad y correlación serial para obtener inferencia válida en modelos estimados por MCO.
properties.rationale: Los errores estándar usuales pueden ser incorrectos si existen correlación serial o heterocedasticidad.

reference.chapter: 12.5 Inferencia robusta a la correlación serial después de MCO

properties.name: Calcular errores estándar robustos a la heterocedasticidad
properties.description: Se recomienda calcular errores estándar robustos cuando se detecta heterocedasticidad en MC2E.
properties.rationale: Los errores estándar convencionales pueden ser incorrectos bajo heterocedasticidad.

properties.name: Especificar cuidadosamente las variables binarias
properties.description: Evitar la colinealidad perfecta seleccionando un grupo base y no incluyendo variables binarias para todos los grupos.
properties.rationale: La colinealidad perfecta impide la estimación de los coeficientes.

properties.name: Usar estadísticos robustos
properties.description: Se recomienda obtener estadísticos de prueba robustos a la heterocedasticidad o correlación serial de formas desconocidas.

properties.name: Evaluar normalidad condicional en regresión
properties.description: En el contexto de regresión, se debe evaluar la normalidad de las distribuciones condicionales de la variable dependiente y sus transformaciones.

properties.name: Evaluate Classifier by Positive Class Success Rate
properties.description: For imbalanced data, focus on the proportion of correctly predicted positives rather than overall error rate.
properties.rationale: Overall error rate can be misleading when the negative class dominates.
examples: Random guessing yields 6% success, KNN yields 11.7%.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evaluate model on a larger test set
properties.description: Assess model performance on a larger test set before drawing conclusions about its effectiveness.
properties.rationale: Small test sets may not provide reliable estimates of model accuracy.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evaluate Model Performance on Independent Test Set
properties.description: Always assess model performance using an independent test set to avoid misleading results from overfitting.
properties.rationale: Training set metrics can be artificially improved by adding variables, but test set metrics reveal true generalization.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evaluate Test Error
properties.description: Always estimate the test error of a classification tree by evaluating its performance on a separate test set rather than relying solely on training error.
properties.rationale: Training error underestimates the true error rate due to overfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evaluate Model Performance with Validation or Cross-Validation
properties.description: Model performance should be assessed using validation set error, cross-validation, or similar methods, not just training error.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Evitar usar pruebas t individuales para hipótesis conjunta
properties.description: No se deben considerar por separado los estadísticos t al probar una hipótesis conjunta, ya que puede llevar a conclusiones equivocadas.
properties.rationale: La prueba F conjunta es más adecuada para evaluar la significancia de varios coeficientes.

properties.name: Use exact=T for least squares coefficients in glmnet
properties.description: When lambda=0 in glmnet, use exact=T in predict() to obtain exact least squares coefficients.
properties.rationale: Otherwise, predict() interpolates over the grid of lambda values and may not return the exact solution.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.6 Lab 2: Ridge Regression and the Lasso

properties.name: Use exact=T in predict() for Least Squares
properties.description: When using glmnet with lambda=0, set exact=T in predict() to obtain exact least squares coefficients.
properties.rationale: Otherwise, predict() interpolates over the grid of lambda values.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.6 Lab 2: Ridge Regression and the Lasso

properties.name: Use exact=T for least squares in glmnet
properties.description: When using glmnet with lambda=0, specify exact=T in predict() to obtain the true least squares coefficients.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.6 Lab 2: Ridge Regression and the Lasso

properties.name: Be aware of numerical approximation in glmnet
properties.description: When lambda=0, glmnet() yields approximate results; use exact=T for more accuracy, though slight discrepancies may remain.
properties.rationale: Numerical approximation can cause small differences between glmnet() and lm() outputs.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Exclude Redundant Dummy Variable
properties.description: When using dummy variables for intervals or categories, exclude one to avoid redundancy with the intercept term.
properties.rationale: Including all dummy variables creates perfect multicollinearity.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Exclude Redundant Predictor in Step Function Regression
properties.description: When fitting step function models, exclude one dummy variable to avoid redundancy with the intercept.
properties.rationale: Including all dummy variables with an intercept causes perfect multicollinearity.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Exclude Sparse Categories
properties.description: Exclude categories with no positive cases from modeling to avoid wide confidence intervals and unreliable estimates.
properties.rationale: No individuals with less than high school education made more than $250,000, resulting in wide confidence intervals.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Restricción de exclusión en la ecuación de selección
properties.description: Se recomienda incluir al menos una variable en la ecuación de selección que no esté en la ecuación de resultado para mejorar la identificación y evitar multicolinealidad.
properties.rationale: La ausencia de una variable exclusiva puede generar alta multicolinealidad y errores estándar elevados.

properties.name: Feature scaling in SVM
properties.description: Use the scale argument in svm() to control whether features are standardized; choose based on application.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Few Components in PCR
properties.description: A small number of principal components may suffice to achieve low cross-validation error, avoiding overfitting.
properties.rationale: Using all components does not reduce dimensionality and may not improve prediction.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Set Degrees of Freedom to a Fixed Number
properties.description: When fitting additive spline models on several variables, it is pragmatic to set the degrees of freedom to a fixed value, such as four, for all terms.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Understand Forward Stepwise Selection Limitations
properties.description: Forward stepwise selection may not find the best model for a given number of predictors because it builds models sequentially and cannot revisit earlier choices.
properties.rationale: If the best two-variable model does not include the variable chosen in the one-variable model, forward stepwise will miss it.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Forward Stepwise Selection for Computational Efficiency
properties.description: Forward stepwise selection is much more computationally efficient than best subset selection, especially when the number of predictors is large.
properties.rationale: Best subset selection requires fitting 2^p models, while forward stepwise selection requires fitting only about p(p+1)/2 models.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Forward Stepwise Selection when n < p
properties.description: Forward stepwise selection is the only viable subset selection method when the number of predictors exceeds the number of samples.
properties.rationale: Backward stepwise selection requires fitting the full model, which is not possible when n < p.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Add Interaction Terms to GAMs
properties.description: Manually include interaction terms or low-dimensional interaction functions in GAMs to capture important variable interactions.
properties.rationale: Additive models may miss significant interactions unless explicitly included.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use GAMs for Non-Linear Relationships
properties.description: GAMs are preferable when modeling non-linear relationships between predictors and response, as they automate the process and improve prediction accuracy.
properties.rationale: Standard linear regression may miss non-linear effects.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Recognize GAM Additivity Limitation
properties.description: GAMs are restricted to additive effects, which may miss important interactions unless interaction terms are added.
properties.rationale: Additivity can limit model flexibility for complex data.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use predict() for GAM objects
properties.description: Use the predict() method to generate predictions from fitted GAM models, similar to lm objects.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Select GAM terms based on statistical tests
properties.description: Use p-values from ANOVA and summary to decide if non-linear terms are necessary for predictors.
properties.rationale: Avoid unnecessary complexity by including only significant non-linear terms.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Good Experimental Design to Avoid Correlated Errors
properties.description: Design experiments to minimize risk of correlated error terms, such as avoiding related individuals or shared environments.
properties.rationale: Uncorrelated errors are crucial for valid inference in linear regression and other statistical methods.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Handle missing values explicitly
properties.description: Use the na.strings option in data import functions and na.omit to manage missing values in R.
properties.rationale: Ensures missing data is properly recognized and handled, preventing analysis errors.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use High Cost for Linearly Separable Data
properties.description: Setting a very high cost parameter ensures no training errors and a narrow margin when classes are linearly separable.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: State Hypotheses About Population Parameters
properties.description: Hypotheses should be stated about population parameters, not sample estimates.
properties.rationale: Sample estimates vary and do not represent the true parameter.

properties.name: Ignorar variables no significativas
properties.description: Variables con estadísticos t pequeños y signos incorrectos pueden ser ignoradas en el análisis práctico.
properties.rationale: Se concluye que las variables son estadísticamente no significativas.

properties.name: Include Period Dummy in Fixed Effects Model
properties.description: To ensure equivalence with the first difference model when T=2, include a dummy variable for the second period in the fixed effects model.
properties.rationale: This aligns the intercepts between both models for proper comparison.

properties.name: Include R-squared and number of observations
properties.description: Always report R-squared and the number of observations in regression tables.
properties.rationale: These statistics are essential for evaluating model fit and sample size.

properties.name: Incluir tendencia temporal en pruebas de raíz unitaria
properties.description: Es recomendable incluir una tendencia temporal en la prueba Dickey-Fuller si la serie muestra una tendencia pronunciada.
properties.rationale: Omitir la tendencia puede inducir sesgos y resultados engañosos.

properties.name: Include time indicator variables
properties.description: Include variables indicating year, and if relevant, quarter or month, when organizing time series data.
properties.rationale: Facilitates identification and analysis of temporal effects.

properties.name: Incluir tendencia si variable independiente tiene tendencia
properties.description: Siempre incluir una variable de tendencia en la regresión si alguna variable independiente muestra tendencia temporal.
properties.rationale: Evita subestimar el efecto de variables independientes con tendencia.

properties.name: Incluir variables binarias anuales
properties.description: Es importante incluir variables binarias anuales para controlar tendencias agregadas en la productividad y evitar atribuir erróneamente efectos a los subsidios.
properties.rationale: Omitir las binarias puede llevar a atribuir el aumento secular en productividad a los subsidios.

properties.name: Incluir intercepto en regresión
properties.description: Se recomienda incluir el intercepto en la regresión para evitar sesgo en los estimadores de pendiente cuando el intercepto poblacional es distinto de cero.
properties.rationale: La omisión del intercepto puede causar sesgo severo en los estimadores de pendiente.

properties.name: Incluir variable binaria anual en regresión
properties.description: Es recomendable incluir una variable binaria para el año en la regresión cuando se usan salarios nominales para evitar errores por inflación.
properties.rationale: El uso de salarios nominales sin ajustar puede inducir a graves errores si no se consideran los diferentes interceptos por periodo.

properties.name: Incluir variables relevantes en el modelo
properties.description: Se recomienda incluir variables relevantes en el modelo para evitar sesgo en el estimador, especialmente cuando el tamaño de la muestra es grande.
properties.rationale: El sesgo por omisión no disminuye con el tamaño de la muestra, mientras que la varianza sí.

properties.name: Incluir variables de control relevantes
properties.description: Agregar variables de control reduce la varianza residual y el error estándar de los coeficientes, mejorando la significancia estadística.
properties.rationale: Las características de la vivienda pueden diferir entre años o ubicaciones, afectando los resultados si no se controlan.

properties.name: Incluir variables independientes que afectan a y y no están correlacionadas con las variables de interés
properties.description: Siempre deben incluirse variables independientes que afectan la variable dependiente y que no están correlacionadas con las variables de interés, ya que reducen la varianza del error sin inducir multicolinealidad.
properties.rationale: Agregar estas variables mejora la precisión de los estimadores sin aumentar la multicolinealidad.

properties.name: Interpretar cuidadosamente los términos de interacción
properties.description: Al analizar modelos con variables de interacción, no se debe interpretar el coeficiente de la variable binaria aisladamente; se deben considerar todas las interacciones.
properties.rationale: La diferencia estimada por la variable binaria solo es válida cuando las variables explicativas son cero, lo cual rara vez ocurre.

reference.chapter: Análisis de regresión con datos de corte transversal

properties.name: Interpret log-linear regression coefficients correctly
properties.description: Interpret the coefficient as the percentage change in wage, not in log(wage), for each additional year of education.
properties.rationale: Misinterpreting the coefficient can lead to incorrect conclusions about the effect of education.

properties.name: Interpret Logistic Regression Coefficients Carefully
properties.description: Logistic regression coefficients represent changes in log odds; interpret them in terms of probability only after transformation.
properties.rationale: Direct interpretation of coefficients can be misleading without converting log odds to probabilities.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Interpretar el MPL cerca de los promedios
properties.description: Las predicciones del modelo de probabilidad lineal son más confiables cuando las variables independientes están cerca de sus valores promedio en la muestra.
properties.rationale: Predicciones extremas pueden estar fuera del intervalo unitario y ser poco interpretables.

properties.name: Interpret p-values carefully
properties.description: A small p-value suggests evidence of association, but values like 0.15 are not considered statistically significant.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 4.6 Lab: Logistic Regression, LDA, QDA, and KNN

properties.name: Interpret Proportion of Variance Explained
properties.description: Assess the importance of principal components by examining the proportion of variance each explains.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Interpret Single Linkage with Caution
properties.description: Single linkage may identify singleton clusters and chaining effects, which can be misleading for group structure.
properties.rationale: Single linkage often results in elongated clusters and may not separate groups correctly.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Interpretación de términos de interacción
properties.description: Verificar la significancia estadística y económica de los términos de interacción antes de incluirlos en la interpretación del modelo.

properties.name: Correct Interpretation of Dendrograms
properties.description: Similarity between observations should be inferred from the vertical axis where branches fuse, not from their horizontal proximity.
properties.rationale: The horizontal order of leaves can be rearranged without changing the meaning of the dendrogram.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Iterative Estimation in AR(1) Models
properties.description: Utilizar esquemas iterativos para estimar modelos AR(1) puede ser útil en muestras pequeñas, aunque en teoría una sola iteración es suficiente en muestras grandes.

properties.name: Compare IV and OLS Variances
properties.description: Always compare the asymptotic variances of IV and OLS estimators; IV variance is always higher unless x and u are uncorrelated and the instrument is strong.
properties.rationale: Weak instruments lead to large IV variance, making OLS preferable when valid.

properties.name: Use jitter() for rug plots
properties.description: Apply jitter() to avoid overplotting when multiple observations share the same value in a rug plot.
properties.rationale: Prevents data points from covering each other, improving plot readability.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Justify variable elimination with F test
properties.description: Use the F test to justify removing groups of variables such as quadratics or interactions.

properties.name: Use large nstart in K-means
properties.description: Always run K-means clustering with a large value of nstart, such as 20 or 50, to avoid undesirable local optima.
properties.rationale: A small nstart may result in the algorithm converging to a poor local minimum.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use large nstart in K-means
properties.description: Always run K-means clustering with a large value of nstart (such as 20 or 50) to avoid undesirable local optima.
properties.rationale: Multiple random initializations reduce the risk of poor clustering results.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Set random seed for reproducibility
properties.description: Set a random seed using set.seed() before running K-means to ensure results are reproducible.
properties.rationale: Reproducibility is important for consistent clustering outcomes.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Compare KNN to Random Guessing
properties.description: Always compare the performance of KNN to random guessing to assess whether the model is finding meaningful patterns.
