properties.rationale: Random guessing provides a baseline; KNN should outperform it to be useful.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Selección adecuada de rezagos
properties.description: La longitud de los rezagos debe determinarse por la frecuencia de los datos y el tamaño de la muestra para asegurar la validez de la prueba Dickey-Fuller aumentada.
properties.rationale: Incluir demasiados rezagos reduce el poder de la prueba; incluir pocos afecta el tamaño y la validez de los valores críticos.

properties.name: Using a large number of trees in bagging does not lead to overfitting
properties.description: Bagging is robust to the number of trees; using a large value of B will not cause overfitting.
properties.rationale: Averaging predictions reduces variance, and error stabilizes as B increases.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Usar un número grande de réplicas bootstrap
properties.description: Elegir un valor grande para m (por ejemplo, 1,000) mejora la confiabilidad del error estándar bootstrap.
properties.rationale: Más réplicas permiten una estimación más precisa del error estándar.

properties.name: Usar muestras grandes para aproximaciones asintóticas
properties.description: Se recomienda tener al menos 1,500 observaciones para justificar la aproximación del teorema del límite central en análisis de regresión.
properties.rationale: Muestras pequeñas pueden no garantizar la validez de la aproximación normal o t.

properties.name: Use Lasso for Model Interpretability
properties.description: The lasso is preferred over ridge regression when model interpretability and variable selection are important, as it produces sparse solutions.
properties.rationale: Sparse models are easier to interpret and may generalize better by excluding irrelevant variables.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Lasso for More Interpretable Models
properties.description: Lasso produces sparse coefficient estimates, making models easier to interpret by selecting only a subset of variables.
properties.rationale: Sparse models are more interpretable and can reveal important predictors.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.6 Lab 2: Ridge Regression and the Lasso

properties.name: Use Lasso for Sparse Models
properties.description: Lasso is preferred when variable selection and model interpretability are important, as it produces sparse coefficient estimates.
properties.rationale: Lasso sets some coefficients exactly to zero, simplifying the model.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 6.6 Lab 2: Ridge Regression and the Lasso

properties.name: Use Lasso for Interpretability
properties.description: Lasso provides a more interpretable model than ridge regression by producing sparse coefficient estimates.
properties.rationale: Sparse models are easier to understand and communicate.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Lasso May Produce Non-Unique Coefficients
properties.description: In certain settings, lasso regression may yield multiple valid solutions for coefficients, especially with correlated predictors.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choosing LDA or QDA Based on Training Size and Covariance Assumption
properties.description: LDA is preferred when training data is limited and variance reduction is crucial; QDA is recommended for large datasets or when class covariance matrices differ.
properties.rationale: LDA has lower variance but higher bias if its assumptions are violated; QDA is more flexible but can suffer from higher variance with small data.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Choosing Between LDA and QDA
properties.description: LDA is preferred when training data is limited and variance reduction is important; QDA is recommended for large datasets or when class covariance matrices differ.
properties.rationale: LDA has lower variance but higher bias if its assumptions are violated; QDA is more flexible but can suffer from higher variance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Limitar dígitos decimales reportados
properties.description: Se debe limitar el número de dígitos reportados después del punto decimal para los coeficientes y errores estándar, evitando la notación científica.
properties.rationale: Mejora la legibilidad y evita reportar números extremadamente grandes o pequeños.

properties.name: Limit Number of Variables in Model
properties.description: Including only a few relevant variables in a model reduces overfitting and improves performance on test data.
properties.rationale: Adding many unrelated features increases variance and test set error.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Limit Polynomial Degree
properties.description: It is unusual to use polynomial degree greater than 3 or 4 to avoid overfitting and strange curve shapes.
properties.rationale: High-degree polynomials can produce overly flexible and unrealistic fits.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Limit Tree Complexity
properties.description: Smaller trees with fewer splits can reduce variance and improve interpretability, though at the cost of some bias.
properties.rationale: Overly complex trees tend to overfit the training data and perform poorly on test sets.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Limit Number of Variables in Model
properties.description: The best model contains at most a few variables, as including too many predictors increases variance and leads to overfitting.
properties.rationale: Careless inclusion of unrelated features can decrease training MSE and increase R2, but harms test set performance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Limit the number of variables in the model
properties.description: The best model contains at most a few variables to avoid overfitting and ensure good performance on test data.
properties.rationale: Including too many predictors increases variance and test set error.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use linear form for proportion or percentage variables
properties.description: Variables such as unemployment rate or percentage passing an exam are often used in linear form to interpret regression coefficients as point percentage changes.
examples: porcentaje de estudiantes que aprueban un examen

properties.name: Use original form for variables measured in years
properties.description: Variables like education, experience, seniority, and age are usually kept in their original units in regression models.

properties.name: Use Linear Kernel for High-Dimensional Data
properties.description: When the number of features is much larger than the number of observations, a linear kernel is often sufficient and avoids unnecessary flexibility.
properties.rationale: High-dimensional data can be easily separated by linear boundaries, making more complex kernels unnecessary.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Linear Kernel for High-Dimensional Data
properties.description: When the number of features is much larger than the number of observations, a linear kernel should be used for SVM.
properties.rationale: Polynomial or radial kernels add unnecessary flexibility in high-dimensional settings.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Prefer Linear Regression for Interpretability
properties.description: Linear regression is often preferred over KNN when interpretability is important, even if KNN has slightly lower test MSE.
properties.rationale: Linear regression models can be described with a few coefficients and provide p-values.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Test Linear vs Non-linear Terms in GAMs
properties.description: Use ANOVA and p-values to assess whether non-linear terms are needed for predictors in a GAM.
properties.rationale: Including unnecessary non-linear terms can overfit and reduce interpretability.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Assess necessity of non-linear terms
properties.description: Use ANOVA tests to determine if non-linear terms significantly improve model fit over linear terms in GAMs.
properties.rationale: Avoid unnecessary model complexity when a linear term suffices.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Linear Function for Year in GAM
properties.description: A linear function for the year variable is sufficient in GAM modeling, as non-linear terms do not improve fit.
properties.rationale: ANOVA and summary tests show no evidence for non-linearity in year.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Linear Function for Year in GAM
properties.description: A linear function for year is sufficient in GAM models for wage prediction; non-linear terms for year are not needed based on ANOVA results.
properties.rationale: ANOVA and p-values show no evidence for non-linearity in year.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use lo() for Modeling Interactions in GAMs
properties.description: Apply lo() in GAM formulas to model interactions between predictors with local regression surfaces.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use logarithms for large integer counts
properties.description: Variables such as population, number of employees, and school enrollment are often log-transformed due to their large integer nature.

properties.name: Use logarithms for positive monetary quantities
properties.description: Variables like salaries, sales, and market value are commonly transformed using logarithms in regression analysis.

properties.name: Prefer Logarithmic Model for Salary
properties.description: The log-linear model is preferred over the linear model for salary because it explains more variation and its parameters are easier to interpret.
properties.rationale: The log model yields a higher R-squared and more realistic parameter interpretation.

properties.name: Transformar ingreso familiar a logaritmo
properties.description: Usar log(faminc) en lugar de faminc puede mejorar el ajuste del modelo y la interpretación de los coeficientes.

properties.name: Usar transformación logarítmica para reducir heterocedasticidad
properties.description: Transformar la variable dependiente a logaritmo suele reducir la heterocedasticidad en modelos de regresión.
properties.rationale: La menor ocurrencia de heterocedasticidad se ha observado en muchas aplicaciones empíricas al usar logaritmos.

properties.name: Log-transform Response Variable
properties.description: Log-transforming the response variable can help achieve a more typical bell-shaped distribution.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Select Appropriate Probability Cutoff in Logistic Regression
properties.description: Choosing a cutoff lower than 0.5 can improve the identification of positive cases when the positive class is rare.
properties.rationale: Default cutoff of 0.5 may miss most positives in imbalanced datasets.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: Lab: Logistic Regression, LDA, QDA, and KNN

properties.name: Use LOOCV Shortcut for Least Squares
properties.description: For least squares regression, use the shortcut formula to compute LOOCV efficiently rather than fitting n models.
properties.rationale: Shortcut reduces computational cost to that of a single model fit.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: LOOCV Preferred Over Validation Set Approach
properties.description: LOOCV yields less biased and more consistent estimates of test error compared to the validation set approach.
properties.rationale: LOOCV uses nearly all data for training and avoids randomness in splits.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Maintain Low p to n Ratio
properties.description: Keep the ratio of parameters to samples low to reduce the risk of overfitting.
properties.rationale: A high p/n ratio increases the likelihood of overfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Lower Probability Threshold in Imbalanced Data
properties.description: Lowering the probability cut-off in logistic regression can improve detection of rare positive cases in imbalanced datasets.
properties.rationale: A standard 0.5 threshold may miss most positive cases when the positive class is rare.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: Lab: Logistic Regression, LDA, QDA, and KNN

properties.name: Use margin as confidence measure
properties.description: The margin can be interpreted as a measure of confidence in classification; larger margins indicate higher confidence.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R
reference.chapter: 9.2.1 Overview of the Support Vector Classifier

properties.name: Evitar asumir conmutatividad en multiplicación matricial
properties.description: La multiplicación de matrices generalmente no es conmutativa; AB no es igual a BA incluso cuando ambos productos están definidos.
properties.rationale: Asumir conmutatividad puede llevar a errores en cálculos y modelos.

properties.name: Medir el ingreso familiar en miles de dólares
properties.description: Para facilitar la lectura y la interpretación de los coeficientes, es mejor medir el ingreso familiar en miles de dólares.
properties.rationale: Reduce el tamaño de los coeficientes y errores estándar, facilitando la interpretación.

properties.name: Minimizar la minería de datos
properties.description: Evitar buscar en numerosos modelos hasta encontrar un resultado significativo y reportar solo ese resultado, para mejorar la validez de la inferencia estadística.
properties.rationale: La minería de datos puede llevar a resultados no robustos y difíciles de interpretar.

properties.name: Excluir observaciones del primer periodo al diferenciar
properties.description: Al calcular primeras diferencias en paneles, se deben marcar como faltantes las observaciones del primer periodo para evitar datos inválidos en el análisis de regresión.
properties.rationale: Evita el uso de diferencias entre unidades distintas, lo que genera observaciones falsas.

properties.name: Representación adecuada de valores faltantes
properties.description: Se recomienda utilizar un símbolo específico, como un punto, para denotar valores faltantes en vez de dejar espacios en blanco o usar valores imposibles.

properties.name: Compare Multiple Model Selection Criteria
properties.description: When selecting a linear model, compare RSS, adjusted R-squared, Cp, and BIC to identify the most appropriate model.
properties.rationale: Different criteria balance fit and complexity differently; using several provides a more robust selection.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Careful Functional Form Specification
properties.description: Decide on the appropriate functional form for variables, including logarithmic transformations and polynomial terms to capture effects.
properties.rationale: Incorrect functional form can misrepresent relationships and lead to poor model fit.

properties.name: Run K-means Multiple Times with Different Initializations
properties.description: Because K-means finds only a local optimum, it is important to run the algorithm several times with different random initial cluster assignments and select the best solution.
properties.rationale: Different initializations can lead to different clustering results; selecting the solution with the smallest objective value improves reliability.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Multiple Predictors in Regression
properties.description: Including all relevant predictors in a regression model helps avoid misleading results due to confounding.
properties.rationale: Single predictor models can yield different results when predictors are correlated.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Naive Strategy: Predict Market Increase Every Day
properties.description: Predicting market increase every day yields similar accuracy to logistic regression in this example.
properties.rationale: The naive approach achieves 56% accuracy, matching the logistic regression model.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Naive Strategy: Predict Market Up
properties.description: A simple strategy of predicting the market will increase every day yields similar accuracy to logistic regression.
properties.rationale: The market increases 56% of the time, matching the model's accuracy.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Natural Splines for Boundary Stability
properties.description: Natural splines produce more stable estimates at the boundaries due to linearity constraints.
properties.rationale: Regular splines can have high variance at the outer range of predictors.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: No aceptar la hipótesis nula cuando no se rechaza
properties.description: Cuando una prueba estadística no rechaza la hipótesis nula, no se debe concluir que se acepta; solo que no hay suficiente evidencia en contra.
properties.rationale: No rechazar H0 no implica que sea verdadera, solo que los datos no ofrecen evidencia sólida contra ella.

properties.name: No desechar observaciones sin analizar sesgo
properties.description: Antes de eliminar observaciones por falta de datos, se debe analizar si esto introduce sesgo en las estimaciones.

properties.name: No eliminar variables relevantes para reducir multicolinealidad
properties.description: Eliminar variables independientes que pertenecen al modelo poblacional puede llevar a sesgo en los estimadores.
properties.rationale: La reducción de multicolinealidad no debe hacerse a costa de omitir variables importantes.

properties.name: No incluir variables constantes en el tiempo en modelos de efectos fijos
properties.description: Variables explicativas que no varían en el tiempo para cada unidad quedan eliminadas por la transformación intragrupal.
properties.rationale: La transformación hace que la variable sea cero para todas las observaciones, impidiendo su estimación.

properties.name: No usar R cuadrada para modelos VI
properties.description: La R cuadrada no debe utilizarse para evaluar modelos con variables instrumentales, ya que la bondad de ajuste pierde importancia.
properties.rationale: En modelos VI, lo relevante es la consistencia del estimador, no el ajuste.

properties.name: Use Non-linear Function for Age in GAM
properties.description: A non-linear term for age is necessary in GAM modeling, as statistical tests show strong evidence for non-linearity.
properties.rationale: Summary and ANOVA tests indicate significant improvement with non-linear age term.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Non-linear Term for Age in GAM
properties.description: A non-linear term for age is required in GAM models for wage prediction, as indicated by significant p-values.
properties.rationale: Statistical tests show strong evidence for non-linearity in age.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: No restar errores estándar directamente
properties.description: No se debe calcular el error estándar de la diferencia de coeficientes restando sus errores estándar individuales.
properties.rationale: Esto puede llevar a errores estándar negativos y resultados incorrectos.

properties.name: Use large nstart in K-means
properties.description: Always run K-means clustering with a large value of nstart, such as 20 or 50, to avoid undesirable local optima.
properties.rationale: Multiple initial cluster assignments reduce the chance of converging to a poor solution.

properties.name: Omit One Dummy Variable and Include Intercept
properties.description: In models with group dummies, include g-1 dummy variables and an intercept to avoid the dummy variable trap.

properties.name: Ordenar datos de panel en filas contiguas

properties.name: Prefer Panel Data for Schools, Cities, Municipalities
properties.description: It is easier to obtain panel data for schools, cities, municipalities, states, and countries than for individuals or firms.

properties.name: Tune SVM Parameters with Cross-Validation

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Preferir modelos más parsimoniosos
properties.description: Los modelos más sencillos son preferibles cuando todo lo demás es igual, ya que la R-cuadrada usual no penaliza la complejidad.
properties.rationale: Modelos más complejos pueden sobreajustar los datos.

properties.name: Select Principal Components via Cross-Validation in Supervised Analysis
properties.description: When using principal components in supervised analysis, treat the number of components as a tuning parameter and select it via cross-validation.

properties.name: Consider Interpretability in PCR

properties.name: PCR Interpretation Limitation
properties.description: PCR models are harder to interpret because they do not perform variable selection or directly produce coefficient estimates.
properties.rationale: Principal components are linear combinations of predictors, making direct interpretation challenging.

properties.name: PCR Does Not Perform Variable Selection
properties.description: PCR does not directly select variables or produce coefficient estimates, making the final model harder to interpret.
properties.rationale: Users should be aware that PCR focuses on dimension reduction rather than interpretability.

properties.name: PCR is not a feature selection method
properties.description: PCR reduces dimensionality but does not select individual features, as each principal component is a linear combination of all original predictors.

properties.description: Visualize the estimated smooth functions and confidence intervals in a GAM using plot.gam().

properties.name: Plot PCA Scores by Group
properties.description: Visualizing principal component scores with group-based coloring helps reveal patterns and similarities among groups.

properties.name: Choosing raw vs. orthogonal polynomials in poly()
properties.description: Using raw=TRUE in poly() returns raw powers; the choice affects coefficient estimates but not fitted values.

properties.name: El error estándar debe ser positivo
properties.description: Los errores estándar siempre deben ser positivos, ya que son estimaciones de desviaciones estándar.
properties.rationale: Un error estándar negativo no tiene sentido estadístico.

properties.description: La única manera de reducir la varianza de los estimadores insesgados en presencia de multicolinealidad es recolectar más datos.

properties.description: Always report model fit statistics (e.g., MSE, R2) on an independent test set or via cross-validation, not on the training set.

properties.description: Los datos deben almacenarse en forma tabular, donde cada observación es una fila y cada variable una columna.

properties.name: Usar tendencias simples en modelos de series de tiempo
properties.description: Se recomienda incluir solo términos de tendencia simples en los modelos para capturar movimientos amplios, evitando sobreajustar con polinomios de alto grado.

properties.name: Test Both Fixed Effects and First Difference Methods
properties.description: It is often recommended to estimate both models and check if results are sensitive to the method chosen.
properties.rationale: Sensitivity to model choice may indicate violation of assumptions or model misspecification.

properties.name: Test Functional Form Before Heteroscedasticity
properties.description: It is better to use explicit tests for functional form misspecification before testing for heteroscedasticity, as misspecification is more critical.
properties.rationale: Misspecified functional form can lead to false positives in heteroscedasticity tests.

properties.name: Probar relevancia de los instrumentos
properties.description: Siempre verificar que los instrumentos estén suficientemente correlacionados con la variable endógena para evitar instrumentos débiles.

properties.name: Modify Classification Threshold

properties.rationale: Adjusting the threshold helps meet business objectives, like minimizing missed defaults for credit card companies.

properties.name: Adjusting Posterior Probability Threshold
properties.description: Changing the threshold for posterior probability allows for more conservative or aggressive classification decisions.

properties.description: Si los resultados cambian significativamente al incluir una tendencia, los resultados iniciales sin tendencia deben considerarse con precaución.

properties.name: Tune Regularization Parameter
properties.description: Carefully select the tuning parameter (e.g., lambda in lasso) to achieve optimal predictive performance.

properties.name: Appropriate Tuning Parameter Selection
properties.description: Careful selection of the tuning parameter is crucial for achieving good predictive performance in regularized models.

properties.name: Uniform Knot Placement
properties.description: In practice, knots are often placed at uniform quantiles of the data to ensure even flexibility across the predictor range.
properties.rationale: Uniform placement avoids overfitting in sparse regions and underfitting in dense regions.

properties.name: Incluir identificador único en datos de panel
properties.description: Es importante incluir un identificador único para cada unidad de corte transversal junto con una variable de año para facilitar el análisis de datos de panel.

properties.name: Usar estadísticos robustos a la heterocedasticidad
properties.description: Se recomienda emplear procedimientos robustos al estimar modelos por MCO cuando existe sospecha de heterocedasticidad.
properties.rationale: Los errores estándar y pruebas de hipótesis tradicionales pueden ser inválidos bajo heterocedasticidad.

properties.name: Usar estimadores MCG factibles en presencia de correlación serial alta
properties.description: Cuando hay alta correlación serial, es preferible usar estimadores como Prais-Winsten o Cochrane-Orcutt en vez de solo corregir los errores estándar de MCO.
properties.rationale: MCO puede ser muy ineficiente en muestras pequeñas con correlación serial.

properties.name: Usar log(salario) como variable dependiente
properties.description: Utilizar el logaritmo del salario como variable dependiente permite que los efectos de los deflactores de precios se absorban en el intercepto.
properties.rationale: Esto simplifica el análisis y evita la necesidad de convertir salarios nominales a reales.

properties.name: Usar MCP en presencia de heterocedasticidad
properties.description: Es preferible usar MCP, incluso si la forma de heterocedasticidad está mal especificada, que ignorarla y usar MCO.
properties.rationale: MCP puede producir estimadores con varianzas menores en casos de fuerte heterocedasticidad.

properties.name: Usar MCP cuando hay heterocedasticidad
properties.description: Se recomienda utilizar mínimos cuadrados ponderados cuando se sospecha que la varianza del error no es constante.
properties.rationale: MCP produce estimaciones eficientes bajo heterocedasticidad.

properties.name: Usar tablas de valores críticos
properties.description: Consultar tablas estadísticas para determinar valores críticos adecuados según el nivel de significancia y grados de libertad en pruebas t y F.
properties.rationale: La correcta identificación del valor crítico es esencial para la interpretación de resultados estadísticos.

properties.name: Usar variables observables en regresión múltiple
properties.description: Modelar la media condicionada sobre variables observables permite estimar efectos ceteris paribus sin depender de proxies para variables no observadas.
properties.rationale: Evita problemas de especificación y simplifica la interpretación.

properties.name: Use Adjusted R2 for Model Selection
properties.description: Adjusted R2 should be preferred over R2 for model selection as it accounts for the number of predictors.
properties.rationale: Prevents overfitting by penalizing the addition of unnecessary variables.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Usar R-cuadrada ajustada para elegir entre modelos no anidados
properties.description: La R-cuadrada ajustada puede ser útil para comparar modelos no anidados y evitar variables redundantes.

properties.name: Usar AR(1) para pronosticar inflación
properties.description: El modelo AR(1) es adecuado para pronosticar la inflación cuando unem&1 no es significativo.
properties.rationale: La inclusión de unem&1 no mejora el modelo para inf.

properties.name: Use Centered R-squared
properties.description: Always calculate R-squared using the centered sum of squares for meaningful goodness-of-fit assessment.
properties.rationale: Uncentered R-squared can be misleadingly high and is rarely appropriate.

properties.name: Use col parameter for color
properties.description: Use col=2 or col='red' to color plots and histograms for better distinction.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation to Select Number of Trees in Boosting
properties.description: Cross-validation should be used to select the number of trees (B) in boosting to avoid overfitting.
properties.rationale: Boosting can overfit if too many trees are used.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation to Select Number of Trees in Boosting
properties.description: Cross-validation should be used to determine the optimal number of trees (B) in boosting to avoid overfitting.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation to Select Cost Parameter
properties.description: Selecting the cost parameter via cross-validation minimizes classification error and improves model performance.
properties.rationale: Different cost values yield different error rates; cross-validation identifies the optimal value.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation for Model Selection
properties.description: Cross-validation provides a reliable estimate of model performance and helps select the optimal model size.
properties.rationale: Avoids overfitting and ensures generalizability.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation for Parameter Selection
properties.description: Selecting SVM parameters such as cost using cross-validation helps prevent overfitting and improves model generalization.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation for SVM Parameter Selection
properties.description: Cross-validation should be used to select the best cost and gamma parameters for SVMs to avoid overfitting and improve test performance.
properties.rationale: Manual selection can lead to overfitting or underfitting; cross-validation provides an objective measure.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use cross-validation to select lambda
properties.description: Instead of arbitrarily choosing lambda, use cross-validation to select the tuning parameter for regularization.
properties.rationale: Cross-validation provides an objective way to minimize test error.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use Cross-Validation for Model Selection
properties.description: Cross-validation error rates provide a good approximation to test error rates and help select optimal model complexity.
properties.rationale: Training error cannot be used to select optimal model complexity as it always decreases with flexibility.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use data argument in lm()
properties.description: Always specify the data argument in lm() to avoid errors related to variable scope.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use exact=T in predict() for glmnet with lambda=0
properties.description: When predicting with glmnet at lambda=0, use exact=T to get exact least squares coefficients.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use extractor functions instead of direct access
properties.description: Prefer extractor functions like coef() over direct access (e.g. lm.fit$coefficients) for reliability.
properties.rationale: Extractor functions are safer and less prone to errors when accessing model components.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use F-statistic for overall association
properties.description: The F-statistic should be used to test for any association between predictors and response to avoid false positives from multiple testing.
properties.rationale: Individual p-values may be misleading when the number of predictors is large.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Use full data set for final model selection

properties.name: Utilizar análisis gráfico para decidir inclusión de tendencia

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use held out data for testing
properties.description: Assess model accuracy using data not used for training to obtain a realistic error rate.
properties.rationale: Training error rate is often overly optimistic and underestimates the test error rate.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Use k-Fold Cross-Validation for Efficiency
properties.description: k-Fold CV is computationally faster than LOOCV for large datasets and provides reliable error estimates.
properties.rationale: k-Fold CV reduces computation time compared to LOOCV, especially when LOOCV formulas are not optimized.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Usar rezagos como instrumentos
properties.description: Utilizar rezagos de segundo orden de las variables como instrumentos para abordar problemas de medición y rezagos en la información.

properties.name: Use large nstart in K-means
properties.description: Always run K-means clustering with a large value of nstart, such as 20 or 50, to avoid undesirable local optima.

properties.name: Use raw=TRUE in poly() for explicit polynomial terms

properties.name: Utilizar errores estándar robustos

properties.name: Use Test Error for Model Evaluation

properties.name: Perform Variable Selection Only on Training Data
properties.description: Variable selection must be performed using only the training set to ensure accurate test error estimates.
properties.rationale: Using the full dataset for variable selection biases validation and cross-validation error estimates.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Incluir variables de control no correlacionadas
properties.description: En un modelo de regresión se deben incluir variables adicionales de control que no estén correlacionadas con la variable explicativa de interés.

properties.name: Usar solo variables observables para predicción
properties.description: Al construir modelos de predicción, se deben incluir únicamente variables que puedan medirse en el momento de la predicción.
properties.rationale: Evita problemas de disponibilidad y asegura la aplicabilidad del modelo.

properties.name: Verificar el formato de proporciones reportadas
properties.description: Revise si las proporciones están reportadas correctamente como porcentajes, especialmente en medios de comunicación.
properties.rationale: Las proporciones pueden ser malinterpretadas si se presentan como porcentajes.

properties.name: Condiciones para una VI válida
properties.description: Una variable instrumental debe estar correlacionada con la variable explicativa pero no con el término de error.
properties.rationale: Solo así puede corregir la endogeneidad y producir estimadores consistentes.

properties.name: Visual Analysis for Component Selection in Unsupervised PCA

properties.name: Estimación de máxima verosimilitud (EMV)

properties.name: Estimación de Prais-Winsten (PW)

properties.name: Estimación de cuasi máxima verosimilitud (ECMV)

properties.name: Estimador

properties.name: MCO cuasi diferenciado
properties.description: Estimador de mínimos cuadrados ordinarios aplicado a datos cuasi diferenciados para eliminar la correlación serial en los errores.

properties.name: Estimador MCO con promedio de mediciones
properties.description: El estimador de MCO usando el promedio de m mediciones de la variable explicativa reduce la inconsistencia causada por el error de medición.

properties.name: Optimal Allocation Fraction (α)
properties.description: Estimator for the fraction of investment in asset X that minimizes portfolio variance, using sample estimates of variance and covariance.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R.pdf

properties.name: Partial Maximum Likelihood Estimator
properties.description: An estimation method that maximizes a portion of the likelihood function, useful in certain econometric models.

reference.book: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data

properties.name: First Difference Estimator (PD)
properties.description: Estimator for panel data models using first differences to remove time-invariant effects; subject to bias if regressors are not strictly exogenous or have measurement error.

properties.name: Poisson Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MLE)
properties.description: Estimador de máxima verosimilitud para el modelo de Poisson, basado en la función de log-verosimilitud.

reference.chapter: Modelos de variable dependiente limitada y correcciones a la selección muestral

properties.name: MCO combinado
properties.description: Estimador de mínimos cuadrados ordinarios aplicado a datos combinados, susceptible a sesgo si hay correlación serial en los errores.

properties.name: Pooled Variance Estimator (σ2)
properties.description: Estimated as a weighted average of sample variances for each class.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Prais-Winsten
properties.description: Estimador que corrige la correlación serial de primer orden en modelos de series de tiempo.

properties.name: Prais-Winsten para Panel
properties.description: Estimador factible que corrige la presencia de correlación serial AR(1) en modelos de panel mediante una transformación basada en el coeficiente estimado.

properties.name: Primera observación (Y1)
properties.description: La primera observación de la muestra es un estimador insesgado de la media poblacional, pero su varianza es igual a la varianza poblacional, mucho mayor que la del promedio muestral.

properties.name: probit
properties.description: Estimador para modelos de respuesta binaria basado en la función de distribución normal.

properties.name: Promedio Muestral (Ȳ)
properties.description: El promedio de variables aleatorias independientes y distribuidas idénticamente, usado para estimar la media poblacional.

properties.name: Promedio Ponderado (W)
properties.description: Estimador de la media poblacional usando ponderaciones distintas para cada variable aleatoria.

properties.name: Proporción de éxitos sobre fracasos
properties.description: El estimador G = Y¯/(1 - Y¯) representa la proporción de éxitos sobre la proporción de fracasos en la muestra.

properties.name: Estimación de cuasi máxima verosimilitud (ECMV)
properties.description: Método de estimación que maximiza una función de cuasi verosimilitud, útil en presencia de sobredispersión.

properties.name: Quasi-Maximum Likelihood Estimator for Poisson
properties.description: Estimador de cuasi máxima verosimilitud (ECMV) para el modelo de Poisson, útil cuando la distribución de Poisson no es completamente correcta.

properties.name: Estimador de efectos aleatorios
properties.description: Estimador utilizado en modelos de panel para capturar la variabilidad entre individuos o entidades.

properties.name: Regression Through Origin Estimator
properties.description: Estimator of $0 obtained as the OLS slope from regressing y on exp(log(y)) without intercept, consistent but not unbiased.

properties.name: Ridge Estimator
properties.description: The coefficient estimator in ridge regression, given by β̂R_j = yj/(1 + λ) in the simple diagonal case.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: RXY
properties.description: Estimador consistente pero sesgado de la correlación poblacional, debido a que es una razón de estimadores y las desviaciones estándar muestrales son sesgadas.

properties.name: Sample Alpha Minimizer
properties.description: Estimator for α using sample estimates of variances and covariance: α̂ = (σ̂²Y - σ̂XY) / (σ̂²X + σ̂²Y - 2σ̂XY).

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Sample Autocorrelation (ˆρ1)
properties.description: An estimator for the first order autocorrelation, consistent under certain conditions but not unbiased.

properties.name: Correlación Muestral
properties.description: Estimador consistente de la correlación poblacional, calculado como la covarianza muestral dividida por el producto de las desviaciones estándar muestrales.

properties.name: Covarianza Muestral
properties.description: Estimador insesgado y consistente de la covarianza poblacional usando n-1 como divisor.

properties.name: Sample Mean
properties.description: The sample mean is used to estimate the population mean and is an unbiased estimator.

reference.book: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with R

properties.name: Estimador de la media muestral para Bernoulli
properties.description: El estimador natural de la probabilidad de éxito en una variable Bernoulli es el promedio muestral, calculado como la proporción de éxitos.

properties.name: Sample Variance
properties.description: An estimator of the population variance calculated as the sum of squared deviations from the sample mean divided by n-1.

properties.name: Estimador consistente de sigma^2
properties.description: El estimador sigma^2 es consistente bajo los supuestos del teorema 5.2, convergiendo en probabilidad al valor poblacional.

properties.name: Estimador de regresión simple
properties.description: Estimador obtenido al correr la regresión de y sobre x1 omitiendo x2.

properties.name: Estimador smearing
properties.description: Estimador utilizado para corregir sesgos en modelos no lineales al transformar predicciones.

properties.name: Three-Stage Least Squares Estimator
properties.description: A traditional estimator for simultaneous equations models, related to GMM.

reference.book: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data

properties.name: Two-Step M-Estimator
properties.description: An estimator obtained by applying M-estimation in two stages, often used when nuisance parameters are present.

reference.book: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data

properties.name: Estimador insesgado
properties.description: Estimador cuyo valor esperado (o media de su distribución de muestreo) es igual al valor poblacional (sin importar el valor poblacional).

properties.name: Estimador insesgado de la varianza del error (!2)
properties.description: Estimador de la varianza del error basado en el promedio muestral de los residuales cuadrados dividido por los grados de libertad (n - k - 1).

properties.name: Estimador insesgado de la varianza del error en series de tiempo
properties.description: El estimador SRC/gl es insesgado para la varianza del error bajo los supuestos ST.1 a ST.5, donde gl = n - k - 1.

properties.name: Biased Estimator of Error Variance
properties.description: SRC/n is a biased estimator for the error variance because it does not account for the constraints imposed by OLS residuals.

properties.name: Estimadores de Componentes de Varianza en Panel
properties.description: Estimadores consistentes de la varianza del efecto inobservable y del término de error, utilizados para calcular el parámetro theta en modelos de efectos aleatorios.

properties.name: Estimador de la varianza del error
properties.description: La varianza del error puede estimarse usando los datos, permitiendo estimar la varianza de los estimadores de los parámetros.

properties.name: Unbiased Estimator of Error Variance
properties.description: An unbiased estimator for the error variance (!2) in simple regression is SRC/(n-2), adjusting for degrees of freedom.

properties.name: Estimador de variables instrumentales (VI)
properties.description: Estimador utilizado cuando existen variables explicativas endógenas y se dispone de instrumentos válidos.

properties.name: Estimador de VI Consistente
properties.description: El estimador de variables instrumentales es consistente si el instrumento no está correlacionado con el término de error.

properties.name: Estimador W1
properties.description: Estimador alternativo de la media definido como [(n-1)/n]Ȳ.

properties.name: Estimador W1 de Razón
properties.description: Estimador insesgado para el parámetro ' definido como el promedio de Yi/Xi sobre la muestra.

properties.name: Estimador W2
properties.description: Estimador alternativo de la media definido como Ȳ/2.

properties.name: W2 = Ȳ/X̄
properties.description: Estimador definido como el cociente de los promedios muestrales de la producción de maíz y los pixeles de maíz.

properties.name: Estimador de Wald
properties.description: Estimador de agrupación para modelos de regresión simple con variable instrumental binaria, calculado como la diferencia de medias entre grupos definidos por la VI.

properties.name: Mínimos Cuadrados Ponderados
properties.description: Método de estimación alternativo a MCO que asigna pesos a las observaciones para corregir heteroscedasticidad.

properties.name: Estimador de White para la varianza bajo heterocedasticidad
properties.description: Estimador válido de la varianza del estimador MCO en presencia de heterocedasticidad, calculado usando los residuales de la regresión.

reference.chapter: Análisis de regresión con datos de corte transversal

properties.name: Errores estándar robustos a la heterocedasticidad (White)
properties.description: Estimador de la varianza de los coeficientes que es robusto a la heterocedasticidad, atribuido a White (1980).

properties.name: Estimador intragrupal (within)
properties.description: Estimador relacionado con el estimador de efectos fijos.

properties.name: Estimador de mínimos cuadrados ponderados (MCP)
properties.description: Estimador usado para ajustar una forma conocida de heterocedasticidad, donde cada residual cuadrado se pondera por la inversa de la varianza (estimada) del error.

properties.name: Y1
properties.description: Estimador insesgado de la media poblacional cuya varianza es constante para cualquier tamaño de muestra.

properties.name: Función de demanda de elasticidad constante
properties.description: Relación log(q) = 4.7 - 1.25 log(p), donde la elasticidad precio de la demanda es -1.25.

properties.name: Ejemplo: Incremento en el impuesto a las ventas en Michigan
properties.description: El incremento del impuesto a las ventas de 4% a 6% puede describirse como un aumento de dos puntos porcentuales o un incremento del 50% en la tasa fiscal.

properties.name: Causal Directed Acyclic Graphs (Pearl)
properties.description: Teoría matemática y gráfica no paramétrica que utiliza nodos (variables) y aristas dirigidas (relaciones causales) para deducir identificabilidad causal y bloqueo de caminos de confusión.

reference.book: Fundamentals of causal inference using R (Brumback)

properties.name: Graduate Econometrics Core & Semiparametric Theory (MIT 14.382 - Chernozhukov)
properties.description: Marco nuclear de econometría asintótica de posgrado enfocado en estimadores de M, regresión cuantílica y de distribución, análisis contrafáctico, GMM no lineal, ecuaciones de Euler y métodos de remuestreo robusto (Wild Bootstrap).

properties.name: Graduate Time Series Analysis & Macroeconometrics (MIT 14.384 - Mikusheva)
properties.description: Marco avanzado de series de tiempo de posgrado enfocado en la identificación estructural en VARs (SVAR), contrastes multivariados de cointegración (VECM Johansen), modelos de estado-espacio con filtro de Kalman y modelos de factores dinámicos.

properties.name: Microeconometría Estructural y de Formas Reducidas (Wooldridge)
properties.description: Enfoque econométrico basado en expectativas condicionales, proyecciones lineales, exogeneidad estricta/secuencial y condiciones de momento poblacionales.

reference.book: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data (Wooldridge)

properties.name: Applied Econometrics & Mostly Harmless Big Data (MIT 14.387 - Angrist & Chernozhukov)
properties.description: Marco de econometría aplicada de posgrado enfocado en identificación causal con efectos heterogéneos (LATE, Angrist) e inferencia en alta dimensión con machine learning ortogonalizado (Double/Debiased ML, Chernozhukov).

reference.chapter: Syllabus & Lecture Notes: LATE and High-Dimensional Big Data

properties.name: Potential Outcomes Framework (Neyman-Rubin)
properties.description: Marco formal que define el efecto causal a nivel individual como el contraste contrafáctico entre resultados potenciales bajo distintos tratamientos: Y(1) - Y(0).

reference.book: Fundamentals of causal inference using R (Brumback)
reference.chapter: Chapter 3: Potential Outcomes and the Fundamental Problem of Causal Inference

properties.name: Econometría Espacial (Anselin / Bivand)
properties.description: Extensión de la econometría lineal que formaliza la dependencia geográfica mediante matrices de pesos espaciales W, modelando spillovers y autocorrelación de errores.

reference.book: An Introduction to Spatial Data Analysis in R (Anselin, Bivand, Pebesma)

reference.book: Time Series Analysis with Applications in R (Cryer & Chan)

properties.name: Augmented IPTW / AIPW (Doubly Robust)
properties.description: Estimador causal semiparamétrico que combina el modelo de propensión con el de resultados; es consistente si al menos uno está bien especificado.
properties.r_syntax: aipw_estimate <- mean(mu1_hat - mu0_hat + (A*(Y - mu1_hat)/ps) - ((1-A)*(Y - mu0_hat)/(1-ps)))
properties.interpretation_guide: Proporciona protección de doble robustez y alcanza la cota de eficiencia semiparamétrica asintótica.

reference.book: Fundamentals of causal inference using R (Brumback)

properties.name: ARIMA (Box-Jenkins)
properties.description: Metodología univariada que integra diferenciación de orden d para lograr estacionariedad con términos autorregresivos (p) y medias móviles (q).
properties.r_syntax: arima(oilfilters, order = c(1, 1, 1), seasonal = list(order = c(1, 1, 0), period = 12))
properties.interpretation_guide: Modela la estacionalidad anual y la autocorrelación de corto plazo de las ventas para pronósticos insesgados.

reference.book: Time Series Analysis with Applications in R (Cryer & Chan)
reference.chapter: Chapter 6, 7 & 10: Model Specification, Estimation and Seasonal Models

properties.name: Differences-in-Differences (DiD)
properties.description: Diseño cuasiexperimental que compara la evolución temporal del resultado entre un grupo tratado y un control antes y después de una intervención.
properties.r_syntax: lm(y ~ treated * post + controls, data = did_data)
properties.interpretation_guide: El coeficiente del término de interacción 'treated:post' captura el efecto causal del tratamiento bajo el supuesto de tendencias paralelas contrafácticas.

reference.book: Introduction to Econometrics with R (Hanck et al.)

properties.name: Distribution Regression & Counterfactual Analysis (Chernozhukov et al.)
properties.description: Método semiparamétrico que estima la función de distribución acumulada condicional completa F_Y|X(y|x) ajustando una serie de modelos binarios en diferentes umbrales, permitiendo descomponer diferencias salariales y efectos de tratamiento en toda la distribución.

reference.chapter: Lecture 7: Distribution Regression and Counterfactual Analysis

properties.r_syntax: counterfactual(formula = log(wage) ~ educ + exper, data = df, group = treat, nreg = 100)
properties.interpretation_guide: Permite descomponer la brecha salarial contrafáctica en efecto composición (características) y efecto estructura salarial (retornos) en cualquier cuantil sin asumir linealidad.

properties.name: Double / Debiased Machine Learning (Chernozhukov et al.)
properties.description: Marco econométrico de frontera que utiliza algoritmos de Machine Learning (Random Forest, Lasso, Gradient Boosting) para estimar funciones nuisance mientras preserva inferencia asintótica estándar raíz-n mediante Ortogonalidad de Neyman y Cross-Fitting.

reference.chapter: Lecture: Double Machine Learning for Treatment and Structural Parameters

properties.r_syntax: dml_plr <- DoubleMLPLR$new(data = obj_dml_data, ml_l = lrn('regr.ranger'), ml_m = lrn('regr.ranger'), n_folds = 5); dml_plr$fit()
properties.interpretation_guide: El coeficiente theta representa el efecto causal estructural desesgado tras purgar de forma no paramétrica las funciones de confusión g(X) y m(X) mediante residuos cruzados ortogonales.

properties.name: Dynamic Panel GMM (Arellano-Bond)
properties.description: Estimador GMM en diferencias y sistema que utiliza rezagos temporales de variables en niveles y diferencias como instrumentos para modelos autorregresivos.
properties.r_syntax: pgmm(log(scrap) ~ lag(log(scrap), 1) + grant | lag(log(scrap), 2:4), data = jtrain, effect = 'individual', model = 'twosteps')
properties.interpretation_guide: Permite modelar persistencia temporal de la tasa de desecho controlando por feedback dinámico y heterogeneidad no observada.

reference.book: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data (Wooldridge)

properties.name: Dynamic Factor Models (Stock & Watson / Bai & Ng)
properties.description: Marco de reducción de dimensión para macroeconomía de alta dimensión donde cientos de series temporales se descomponen en una combinación lineal de pocos factores comunes latentes f_t y componentes idiosincráticos e_it.

reference.chapter: Lecture 14 & 15: Large Factor Models and PCA

properties.r_syntax: prcomp(macro_matrix, scale. = TRUE)
properties.interpretation_guide: Los factores estimados sintetizan las condiciones macroeconómicas generales y mejoran radicalmente el pronóstico de inflación y actividad económica.

properties.name: Fixed Effects (Within Panel Estimator)
properties.description: Transformación intragrupos que resta la media temporal de cada entidad para eliminar la heterogeneidad individual no observable constante en el tiempo c_i.
properties.r_syntax: plm(mrall ~ beertax + vmiles, data = Fatalities, index = c('state', 'year'), model = 'within')
properties.interpretation_guide: Controla por factores fijos estatales no medidos (geografía, cultura vial); el efecto del impuesto a la cerveza sobre fatalidades viales se identifica a partir de la variación intra-estatal a lo largo del tiempo.

reference.book: Introduction to Econometrics with R (Hanck et al.)

properties.name: Front-Door Method (Pearl / Brumback)
properties.description: Método de identificación causal que explota un mediador M exhaustivo y no confundido con Y para identificar el efecto de X sobre Y en presencia de confusión no observada.
properties.r_syntax: # Dos pasos de estandarización: X -> M y M -> Y

properties.name: Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (Fuzzy RDD)
properties.description: Diseño cuasiexperimental donde la probabilidad de recibir el tratamiento salta discontinuamente en un umbral c pero sin alcanzar 0 o 1. Se estima como un modelo de variables instrumentales locales donde el corte sirve de instrumento.

reference.chapter: Lecture: Regression Discontinuity: Sharp vs Fuzzy

properties.r_syntax: rdrobust(y = outcome, x = score, c = threshold, fuzzy = treatment)
properties.interpretation_guide: Estima el efecto LATE en el entorno inmediato del umbral de corte (cutoff) para los individuos cuya condición de tratamiento fue modificada por cruzar dicho umbral.

properties.name: GARCH (Volatilidad Condicional)
properties.description: Modelo para series temporales financieras donde la varianza condicional de los retornos depende de shocks cuadráticos pasados y varianzas pasadas.
properties.r_syntax: garch(cref, order = c(1, 1))
properties.interpretation_guide: La suma de los coeficientes alpha_1 + beta_1 mide la persistencia de los choques de volatilidad en el mercado financiero.

reference.chapter: Chapter 12: Time Series Models of Heteroscedasticity

properties.description: Estandarización causal que ajusta un modelo de regresión para el resultado y predice contrafácticamente fijando el tratamiento en 1 y 0.
